title: soft-degradation: priority queues + fallback execution policy for SLO-critical routes
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: several incidents over the past quarter showed that binary drop/allow load-shedding causes unacceptable SLO regressions for high-priority customers and noisy neighbor effects for bursty inference workloads. This PR introduces a soft-degradation execution path that preserves latency SLOs for SLO-tagged traffic while allowing best-effort degradation for low-priority work. The approach combines per-route priority queues, headroom tokens, and a lightweight fallback executor that runs model-lite variants or cached responses when the main runtime is congested.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a per-request priority label that can be set via x-redwood-priority header or inferred from token quotas.
- Implements a priority queue scheduler in the serving proxy: high/normal/low queues with configurable time-to-serve thresholds.
- Introduces "headroom tokens" per GPU worker group to reserve capacity for SLO-critical requests; headroom is replenished on request completion and decays under sustained load.
- Adds a fallback execution policy: when a request exceeds its time-to-serve threshold, the scheduler routes it to a fallback executor which can: a) serve from prefix KV cache, b) call a quantized model shard with a reduced max_tokens, or c) return a guarded canned response indicating transient degraded fidelity.
- Provides operator toggles and rate limits: per-tenant priority caps, global fallback ratio, and emergency circuit-breaker to cut fallbacks entirely.
- Adds metrics and tracing spans for priority queue depth, headroom utilization, fallback invocations, and per-tenant degradation rates.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4873)
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler and fallback routing
- [x] Integration tests in perf-canary using synthetic overload patterns
- [x] Feature flag gating + rollout configuration in Console
- [x] RBAC update to allow ops to change priority caps

Risk and mitigation: The main risk is introducing scheduling jitter under mixed workloads. Mitigations included tight end-to-end latency SLO tests, conservative default configs, and a toggle to revert to legacy load-shedding instantly via emergency circuit-breaker.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout behind feature flag: start with internal customers (10% of traffic), monitor headroom/utilization and fallback rate. If stable, increase to 50% then global. Automated SLO regression alerts will rollback the flag.

Related: SUP-1122 (support ticket reporting noisy neighbor latency spikes), ENG-4898 (observability dashboard for degradation metrics).

review_comments:
Arjun Patel: Nice clear design. Two nits: 1) prefer exponential decay for headroom tokens rather than linear to avoid oscillation; 2) add tenant-scoped unit tests.

Maya Chen: addressed both; switched to exponential decay and added tenant-scoped tests in f2a88be.

Sofia Martinez: Can we avoid exposing x-redwood-priority as an arbitrary header from public clients? Suggest map header values to vetted priorities in gateway.

Maya Chen: updated gateway mapping and added validation; only values (high, normal, low) accepted. SDK helper added to set safely.

Liam O'Connor: How will this interact with existing circuit breakers? If fallback starts returning canned responses, operator shouldn't see errors bubble up as 5xx.

Maya Chen: fallback responses are 200 with a response-metadata header x-redwood-degraded:true and a trace tag. Circuit-breaker thresholds unchanged; we added a new metric fallback_rate for alerting.

CI Bot: lint check failed on first run (gofmt).

Maya Chen: fixed formatting and force-pushed; CI passed on second run.
merge_summary: Squash and merge. Commit message summarizes feature, risk mitigations, and rollout plan. Feature gated behind runtime.feature.soft_degradation. Ops runbook added to docs/operations/soft-degradation.md.
release_notes: Added soft-degradation priority queues and fallback executor to improve SLO preservation under congestion. Configurable headroom tokens and per-tenant priority caps. Backwards-compatible and feature-flag gated.
notes_for_ops: 1) Default config is conservative; monitor metrics/redwood.degradation.fallback_rate and metrics/redwood.headroom.utilization. 2) To disable, flip runtime.feature.soft_degradation=false or set fallback_ratio=0. 3) Emergency circuit-breaker toggle available in Console -> Runtime -> Fallbacks.
